the adsorption from mixed surfactant/proteine solutions is described by a simple thermodynamic model.
the thermodynamic model is capable of describing competitive adsorption from mixed solutions.
the adsorption of globular and flexible proteins from mixed solutions with nonionic surfactants can be described by a thermodynamic model which includes the possibility of changing of the molar area.

the adsorption from mixed surfactant/proteins solutions.
the thermodynamic description of the competitive adsorption from mixed solutions of nonionic surfactants and proteins.
the competitive character of adsorption from protein/surfactants mixed systems.

the adsorption from mixed surfactant/proteins is a very complex process which cannot be described by a simple model.

the adsorption of proteins from mixed surfactant/proteins solutions is a very complex process which is influenced by a large number of parameters, such as the type and concentration of surfactant and protein, the pH and ionic strength of the solution, and the temperature.
the adsorption of proteins and surfactants from mixed solutions is a complex process which can be described by a thermodynamic model if the molar area is known as a function of protein concentration.

the thermodynamics of protein adsorption can be described with the same level of accuracy as that for surfactant adsorption, if one takes into account the competitive character of adsorption from a mixture of surfactant and protein.
